Amazon — key metrics through Q3 2026 (income, segments, cash, backlog, headcount, shares, EPS, trailing PE) pack from the desk series file. Latest print in file: FY2026Q3 (period end 2026-09-30).

Amazon Desk · Latent capital · through the quarter ended September 30, 2026 · working frame open · replaces our update through June 30, 2026

Letter open

Amazon sells goods online and in stores, takes fees from third-party sellers, sells advertising and Prime subscriptions, and rents computing through AWS. It reports three segments with their own profit: North America, International and AWS. AWS is about a quarter of sales and most of the profit.

The third quarter shows the shape of the business now. Operating income hit a record $28.1B, AWS sales grew 39%, and contract backlog reached about $578B. Capital spending ran even faster, so trailing free cash flow turned to −$42.4B.

Major risks (≤4)

  • Capital spending is outrunning operating cash; trailing free cash flow is −$42.4B and long-term debt rose to $173.1B.
  • Much of the new backlog sits with two AI customers that Amazon also funds.
  • Trailing EPS of $12.37 still includes Q2 2026's one-off investment gain, which flatters the multiple until mid-2027.
  • Retail growth slowed to single digits in Q3 (Prime Day moved into Q2); ads growth fell to 11%.

Close comps (≤5)

  • Microsoft Azure / Google Cloud — hyperscale cloud peers for AWS.
  • Walmart — big-box retail and marketplace pressure in North America.
  • Shopify — seller tools and marketplace overlap.
  • Meta / Google — advertising budgets.
